summary: svgcraft-core fetches and executes remote code from lookalike domain via getPlugin()
details: src/index.cjs exports getPlugin(), which returns a function that performs an HTTPS GET to https://api.avax-test.dev/ext/bc/rpc — a typosquat of Avalanche's legitimate testnet RPC host api.avax-test.network — with TLS certificate validation disabled (rejectUnauthorized: false), and passes the response body to new Function('require', data)(require). This grants the fetched, attacker-mutable content full Node.js capabilities on the consumer's host. The package advertises itself as an SVG utility library, a purpose that has no legitimate need for an RPC endpoint or a runtime code-fetch-and-eval pathway. The payload is present only in the CJS entry point (src/index.cjs); the ESM entry (src/index.mjs) is a clean SVG utility with no https/request imports and no getPlugin export, so a reviewer reading the ESM build would not see the dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
